251: ## 6. Input mapping
252: 
253: | action | Vision Pro | Quest (hands / controllers) | Laptop |
254: |---|---|---|---|
255: | focus / inspect tile | gaze + pinch (select) → detail plane | pinch / trigger on tile | click |
256: | pipe | pinch-hold tile, carry, release over another column (0.5 m radius) | same | drag tile onto column, or select + P + click |
257: | fork | pinch-hold title plate, pull > 0.5 m sideways, release | same | F on selected column (lands 0.8 m right) |
258: | move column | pinch-hold base, drag on floor | same | drag base; T = top-down view |
259: | summon (local) | pinch-hold base 0.6 s without moving | same | S (or double-click column) |
260: | scroll history (local) | pinch-hold stack, move vertically | same; thumbstick | mouse wheel over column; Home |
261: | push-to-talk | left pinch while left ray hits mic sphere/nothing | left pinch / left squeeze | hold Space |
262: | approve | look at the red column, say "yes, go ahead" (voice) or select the beacon → approve | same | Approve/Deny buttons |
263: | recenter height | pinch-hold floor 1 s | same | C |
264: | other keys | — | — | Enter send · Shift+Enter newline · 1–5 cues · R reset · D debug · V spectator · Esc close detail |

message.text:
54: - **Apple Vision Pro (visionOS 2+) Safari**: WebXR is **on by default** (no feature flag since visionOS 2). Supports
55:   `immersive-vr` only (**no `immersive-ar` / passthrough via WebXR**). Input: **transient-pointer** (gaze + pinch; a ray
56:   appears only while pinching) and optional **hand-tracking** (permission prompt; hands are pose-only, no events).
57: - **Meta Quest 3S Browser**: WebXR `immersive-vr` and `immersive-ar` (passthrough) both work; hand tracking + controllers.
58:   **Web Speech API `SpeechRecognition` is NOT exposed in Quest Browser** (developer reports). `getUserMedia` mic capture
59:   works → stream audio to a server for STT (AssemblyAI realtime) as the voice path on Quest.
message.summary: → platform facts: VP immersive-vr only; Quest has no Web Speech

message.text:
write_file {
  "path": "README.md",
  "content": "# cEverything — every AI-agent chat you have open stands as a column in your room

Walk up to a column to read it, look at it and speak to steer it, drag a message from one column to another to connect them — while your laptop teammate types, approves and arranges in the very same room.

## What the judge sees

- One wireframe column per Hermes session, up to ten, on an arc around you.
- Bars from afar, one-line summaries at two metres, full text when you step in.
- Packets fly to three landmarks: the browser pylon, the terminal pylon, the codebase tree.
- A red pulsing ring means a session needs you.

## Run it

    npm install
    npm start                      # fixture replay on http://localhost:8787
    npm run start:tls              # self-signed HTTPS for headsets on the LAN
    HERMES_DASHBOARD=http://127.0.0.1:9119 npm run start:hermes   # live

Flags: --port, --host, --tls, --source fixture|hermes, --fixture fixtures/demo, --speed 4, --no-loop, --public-url.

## Two devices, one room

The laptop person types, reads diffs flat, approves and arranges the floor plan. The headset person glances, walks, looks-and-speaks, pipes and forks. Both mirror one scene held by the Node hub.

## Controls

| action | headset | laptop |
|---|---|---|
| inspect tile | gaze + pinch | click |
| pipe | pinch-hold tile, drop on column | drag tile onto column |
| fork | pull the title plate sideways | F |
| move column | pinch-hold base, drag | drag base, T for top-down |
| talk | hold left pinch / squeeze | hold Space |

## Honesty label

The floor says FIXTURE REPLAY or LIVE: hermes@host. It is in every shot.

## Credits

three.js, ws, qrcode-terminal, AssemblyAI streaming, promptclickrun/bighelp (tool categories).
"
}

message.text:
206: ## 4. Hermes live adapter (server/sources/hermes.js)
207: 
208: Env: `HERMES_DASHBOARD=http://127.0.0.1:9119`, `HERMES_API=http://127.0.0.1:8642`, `HERMES_API_KEY`, `HERMES_PROFILE?`.
209: Read: `GET /api/sessions?order=recent&limit=12` at 1 Hz → `session.upsert`/`session.status`; for each listed session
210: `GET /api/sessions/{id}/messages?order=latest&limit=60` at 1 Hz (stagger), diff by row `id`, run `normalize.js`, emit
211: `message.add` + `tool.start`/`tool.complete`. Optional `ws://…/api/ws` (loopback, no ticket): after `gateway.ready` send
212: `client.capabilities {server_requests:false}`, then map `event` notifications `message.delta`/`reasoning.delta` → `message.delta`
213: on `<sid>:live` / `<sid>:live:r` streaming messages, `tool.start`/`tool.complete` → the same kinds. On any failure the adapter
214: logs once, keeps polling, and sets `sourceInfo.label = "LIVE (polling only)"`. Writes: `send` → `POST /api/sessions/{id}/chat`
215: `{message}`; `fork` → `POST /api/sessions/{id}/fork`; `new` → `POST /api/sessions`. No API key → `error source_unavailable`
message.summary: → §4 live adapter: env, 1 Hz polling, WS optional, polling-only fallback

    HERMES_DASHBOARD=http://127.0.0.1:9119 HERMES_API=http://127.0.0.1:8642 HERMES_API_KEY=… npm run start:hermes

}

  "path": "README.md",
  "old_string": "Fixture sessions are hand-authored and contain no real credentials; the live adapter redacts anything that looks like a secret before it is broadcast.

## Credits",
  "new_string": "Fixture sessions are hand-authored and contain no real credentials; the live adapter redacts anything that looks like a secret before it is broadcast.

### What we claim / what we don't

- "Gaze" means **head gaze** (camera forward) everywhere; we do not use eye tracking. On Vision Pro the pinch ray *is* eye-directed, and that is what targets.
- The Vision Pro path (transient pointers, mic inside immersion) is unverified until it is tested on the device; the Quest path is the one rehearsed.
- Every voice path needs internet (AssemblyAI or Chrome's recognizer). Without it the keyboard is the floor, and the narration says "voice via laptop".

## Credits"
}
